Each /afk:review round, before its concern fan-out, runs one /afk:investigate Q2 per changed public symbol with --out in the review's scratch directory and hands the reviewers the ledger paths (skills/afk/review/SKILL.md:38), and /afk:investigate fans out one afk-tracer per cluster (skills/utils/investigate/SKILL.md:44): every Step 10 and PF-3 round also starts a tracer wave, and ledgers in the review's scratch reach every concern worker.

CLAUDE.md:160 already omits a writer of plan/review/ at HEAD: in a ledger-only round the implementor remediates review reports, INDEX.md and PATTERN-DEBT.md in place (skills/afk/review/SETTLEMENT.md:28; skills/afk/execute/SKILL.md:81).

By ADR-0013's own test a helper subagent is an agent that only reads and returns text to its parent (docs/afk/agent-team-topology/adr/requirements/0013-role-agents-are-pane-agents.md:8), which is what today's concern workers do (skills/afk/review/SKILL.md:110), yet S-208 (docs/afk/agent-team-topology/GRILL-LOG.md:560) lists them among the role-agent spawns: the settled record classifies the workers both ways.

In review-only mode /afk:settle-change writes only scratch and GitLab notes (skills/utils/settle-change/SKILL.md:125) and maps plan/review/ to the MR (skills/utils/settle-change/SKILL.md:49), so its worker result files can only live in scratch.
DELEGATION.md:36 already sanctions one wake that is not a child's completion, the stall watchdog's exit, so a finished-message wake would be a second such source beside it.

GLOSSARY.md already carries the team vocabulary at HEAD (Transport at GLOSSARY.md:35, Lifespan at GLOSSARY.md:42), and its Lifespan entry reads 'a turn, a phase, or a feature' while the settled start check accepts only Turn, Step or Feature (docs/afk/agent-team-topology/GRILL-LOG.md:539, docs/afk/agent-team-topology/GRILL-LOG.md:663).

DELEGATION.md:68 already sends bulk evidence to a file in the run's artifact dir with the return carrying the path, which fits a pane worker that writes its result file and sends finished with the path; under the subagent fallback review workers still return their findings as text (docs/afk/agent-team-topology/PRD.md:144; docs/afk/agent-team-topology/GRILL-LOG.md:561), so DELEGATION.md:65's findings-JSON return tail still binds them.

Today /afk:review starts its concern workers as one fresh subagent per concern, all spawned in one message through the harness's general review role; each prompt pastes checklists/PRECEDENCE.md and the concern's checklist verbatim through the end of its ## Reviewer checklist section with any trailing ## Guardrails block excluded, plus the resolved input paths and the findings contract; the line states 'the subagent has no other access to these files'.

Each concern worker returns its findings as a JSON array in its spawn result; the review orchestrator merges them, dedups by file:line, assigns r-001..r-NNN, writes the report and the ...findings.json file under plan/review/, upserts plan/review/INDEX.md, and returns one REVIEW: line to the caller.

The skeptic wave runs inside /afk:review after merge and dedup: one fresh skeptic per design-level finding of severity medium or above, all spawned in one message, each given the finding, the diff and the CLAUDE.md-chain and spec paths, returning upheld, downgraded (<reason>) or refuted (<reason>).

The adjudicator wave runs in the caller's settle loop, not in /afk:review: after the implementor disputes findings (SETTLEMENT.md step 4) the referee spawns one fresh subagent per disputed finding in one parallel message, handing the finding as verbatim JSON and the implementor's rationale as text plus the diff, contract/spec and CLAUDE.md-chain paths; each returns withdrawn(<reason>) or stands(<reason>).

Reachers of the waves: /afk:execute Step 10 and /afk:preflight PF-3 run /afk:review per round with --tag r{n} as the settle loop's referees; /afk:autopilot reaches Step 10 through the executor subagent it starts, which spawns the review and adversary gates, and reaches PF-3 by invoking /afk:preflight itself on smoke-green, so PF-3 runs in the autopilot session; /afk:settle-change runs the same machinery exactly through its own substitution map and is reached also through the deprecated /afk:settle-mr alias; and a standalone /afk:review {NNNN-slug} audits a slice on demand with the same report and no gating.

No test pins how the waves start, are briefed or return: the search over every tracked tests directory for findings.json, outcomes.json, REVIEW:, r-NNN ids, plan/review, "review", SETTLEMENT and checklists returned only mission-control fixtures, and a case-blind pass for outcome, finding and rollup added only mission-control's rollup assertion and tests of other subjects; the pinned review readers are mission-control's rollup (test_contract.py:317) and round parsing (test_contract.py:519).

claims.text: review/SKILL.md:43 cuts each checklist at the end of ## Reviewer checklist and excludes trailing ## Guardrails blocks; four checklists carry a Guardrails digest (api-contract.md:26, design-quality.md:37, domain-alignment.md:26, resilience.md:25), test-veracity.md carries its ## Mutation probe section after its checklist (:23), and five concern files carry no ## Reviewer checklist heading (claude-md-compliance, logic-correctness, refactor-safety, scope-and-impact, spec-fidelity).

Under a brief of paths only each worker reads PRECEDENCE.md and its checklist file itself, so the Guardrails digests and test-veracity's Mutation probe section reach it unless its brief or role says where to stop; the paste cuts the Mutation probe section today although the probe is the test-veracity worker's job, so the change also decides whether the probe runs.

review/SKILL.md:25 appends --tag to every artifact basename the run writes and says the tag never appears in any reviewer prompt; SETTLEMENT.md:52 forbids the round number in any reviewer, adjudicator or fixer prompt.

A worker result file under plan/review/ is an artifact the run writes, so review/SKILL.md:25 as written would tag it with r{n}, and the path the worker's brief names would carry the round number SETTLEMENT.md:52 forbids; worker result paths, and any brief file holding a finding or a rationale for skeptics and adjudicators, need names without the round tag.

Readers of plan/review/ files: mission-control, preflight, understand and retro select them by name - *.outcomes.json (progress.py:141, preflight/SKILL.md:95 and :162, understand/SKILL.md:49), *.findings.json (retro/SKILL.md:26-27), *-adversary.md (gates.py:8, retro/SKILL.md:29), *.md (understand/SKILL.md:49), INDEX.md and PATTERN-DEBT.md by exact name (insights.py:83, :178) - and PF-3 resolves each deferred finding against its findings file (preflight/SKILL.md:96). One reader does not select by name: a scope-escalated round widens every reviewer's reading surface to the review records the loop has written (review/SKILL.md:102), which consistency-sweep lists as reports, INDEX.md, PATTERN-DEBT.md and JOURNAL.md (consistency-sweep.md:11).

Avoiding the readers' names does not keep worker result files from every reader: on a scope-escalated round every reviewer reads the review records the loop has written (review/SKILL.md:102), which include reports (consistency-sweep.md:11), and the feature's PRD calls a worker's result its report file (PRD.md:144), so raw pre-merge results - findings the skeptic wave dropped included (review/SKILL.md:146) - would reach later escalated reviewers, against the feature's settled rule that only a result file's report target reads it, held by convention because no program can see a file read (GRILL-LOG.md:674, PRD.md:174; working tree). The escalated reading surface must exclude result files, or the files live outside plan/review/. The name-selecting readers stay unchanged while result files avoid their names; a findings array saved as *.findings.json would collide with retro's criterion join and the understanding artifact's id-join, which expect merged findings carrying r-NNN ids.

execute/SKILL.md:135 requires every verdict to be read from the spawning call's own result and forbids waiting on a completion notification from a child, because a subagent's own children do not notify it reliably; DELEGATION.md:34 states that only completion re-invokes a waiting orchestrator.

A review orchestrator that waits for its workers' finished messages is the wait execute/SKILL.md:135 forbids, so that rule and DELEGATION.md:34 must name finished-message delivery as a sanctioned wake source, delivered by a mechanism the idle orchestrator receives.

New reviewer agents with lifespan Turn, requested afresh each round, keep SETTLEMENT.md:8 ('fresh ... never persistent across rounds'); INV-019's lead that a pane role living across rounds breaks that line does not apply, because this change requests no agent that outlives its round.

The skeptic and adjudicator waves cannot be one start request: skeptics run inside /afk:review right after merge, while adjudicators need disputes that exist only after the review pass returns and the implementor answers; settle-change already runs them as separate waves. Each wave as its own start request listing all of its agents keeps today's one-message fan-out.

/afk:settle-change inherits every change to the waves - it runs review's machinery exactly - but maps plan/review/ to the MR with no outcomes files and pastes checklists into reviewer prompts, so the change needs a settle-change row saying where worker result files go.

No writable reviewer role is needed: the feature's settled record runs spawned agents with permissions bypassed and enforces no limit on them (GRILL-LOG.md:35, :54), and in the subagent fallback a role agent returns its report as text and the agent that started it writes the report file (PRD.md:144, working tree). What still changes is review/SKILL.md:12's 'strictly read-only', which a pane worker writing its own result file no longer meets.
The Stop gate refuses skill prose naming SendMessage or subagent_type and prose naming a harness, so the rewritten review prose must name the plugin's own start-request and finished verbs.

The repository does not settle whether an autopilot executor's review waves run inline or as fresh subagents today: autopilot/SKILL.md:35 says the executing subagent spawns its review and adversary gates, while DELEGATION.md:29 says a child whose spawn states no depth runs its helper work inline, and the executor's spawn prompt states none (SUBAGENT-PROMPT.md:3). Start requests depend on the requester: the feature's start check refuses one whose requester is not a live agent in the run manifest (GRILL-LOG.md:626, PRD.md:109, ADR-0016:17; working tree), and a native subagent is never in the manifest (GRILL-LOG.md:371), so an executor autopilot starts as a subagent (autopilot/SKILL.md:33) cannot request its review waves; the review change needs the executor started as a pane agent (ADR-0013).

claims.text: The documents name what reaches the waves. CLAUDE.md:135 says /afk:execute Step 10 and /afk:preflight PF-3 both run /afk:review inside the settle loop. S-208 (docs/afk/agent-team-topology/GRILL-LOG.md:560) adds /afk:settle-change as a third spawner of concern workers, beside /afk:review's workers, skeptics and settle-loop adjudicators.

Worker result files under plan/review/ will be read by agents that are not their report target, whatever the files are named. In a scope-escalated round every reviewer reads 'the review records the loop has written' (skills/afk/review/SKILL.md:102; skills/afk/review/SETTLEMENT.md:35). The consistency-sweep checklist lists those records by kind, reports included, not by name (skills/afk/review/checklists/consistency-sweep.md:11). A name outside the other readers' patterns keeps out only those readers: retro reads *.findings.json and *.outcomes.json (skills/afk/retro/SKILL.md:26-27), understand reads review/*.md and *.outcomes.json (skills/afk/understand/SKILL.md:49), PF-4d reads *.outcomes.json (skills/afk/preflight/SKILL.md:162), and mission control globs *-adversary.md and {subtask}-*.outcomes.json (gates.py:110, insights.py:204, progress.py:141). docs/afk/agent-team-topology/PRD.md:174 lets only the report target read a result file, and S-223 (docs/afk/agent-team-topology/GRILL-LOG.md:626) and ADR-0016 record that nothing detects another agent's read. So either the escalated reading surface leaves out worker result files, or the access rule admits escalated reviewers.

A worker that writes its own result file meets the gate rules as corrected. PD-GATE (docs/afk/agent-team-topology/GRILL-LOG.md:167) and AC-038 (docs/afk/agent-team-topology/PRD.md:138) let a gate worker write its own report file that the gate names, never the gate's other files or status. AC-045 (docs/afk/agent-team-topology/PRD.md:145) keeps merge and numbering with the review orchestrator. Three statements of the review skill change: 'strictly read-only' (skills/afk/review/SKILL.md:12), 'The reviewers are read-only' (skills/afk/review/SKILL.md:38), and 'the subagent has no other access to these files' (skills/afk/review/SKILL.md:43). A brief of paths only makes the last one false, since the worker then reads the checklist file itself. The hard rule at skills/afk/review/SKILL.md:194 (never edit, commit, push or fix) can stay: the skill already writes its own records under plan/review/ (skills/afk/review/SKILL.md:157; CLAUDE.md:160).

The repository states where job scratch lives (PROVIDERS.md:29), that the tracker server is plugin-scoped (PROVIDERS.md:30), that plugin parts activate only through the harness enable flag (PROVIDERS.md:39-40), and the plugin_mcp and plugin_job_dir rows (CAPABILITIES.md:17-18). So a brief of paths only names checklist paths under that root. Whether a pane agent's session may read that root and the review's scratch still needs the live trial the SDD names.

Unverified, pane transport runtime: how a busy pane takes several typed finished messages. Finished messages reach the review orchestrator in its pane, one per worker (S-189, docs/afk/agent-team-topology/GRILL-LOG.md:541; S-215, docs/afk/agent-team-topology/GRILL-LOG.md:618; AC-046, docs/afk/agent-team-topology/PRD.md:146), where today one parallel spawn returns every result. The settled record does say how a wave ends when a worker is lost. The contact agent moves a started agent that ends without finished to lost and sends the requester a message naming it (S-173, docs/afk/agent-team-topology/GRILL-LOG.md:525). A step ends when every agent it started has sent finished or is lost (R46-PATFIELD, docs/afk/agent-team-topology/GRILL-LOG.md:663). So the merge can start when the step ends; only the pane's handling of several messages stays runtime.

CLAUDE.md:135 also holds a findings-JSON lockstep, copied at AGENTS.md:135: plan/review/*.outcomes.json and /afk:retro's criterion-yield mining share the findings 'criterion' and 'id' fields, and widening that shape touches execute Step 10, preflight PF-3 and retro's mining table in the same commit. The change moves each worker's findings array into a result file under plan/review/. The orchestrator assigns the r-NNN ids only when it merges the arrays (skills/afk/review/SKILL.md:110). retro counts every plan/review/*.findings.json and joins it with *.outcomes.json on the finding id (skills/afk/retro/SKILL.md:26-27). A worker file named *.findings.json would be counted beside the merged file, with ids the merge has not assigned. So a worker file needs a name retro does not match. If the worker file's shape is to differ from the merged findings, this lockstep applies as well.

Mission-control counts settle rounds from file names only: its progress section globs plan/review/{subtask}-*.outcomes.json and takes the round number from a name ending -r{n}.outcomes.json (skills/afk/mission-control/scripts/mc/sections/progress.py:26, :141-144), and skills/afk/mission-control/scripts/tests/test_contract.py:514-519 pins that parse. A worker result file under plan/review/ enters the board's round count only through that suffix.
